tidbit: Did you know… one story this hour was carried by two different outlets in the last few hours.
transcript:
Hourly brief, Founders' Preview. Here is what is moving in superintelligence (SI), the next generation of artificial intelligence (AI).
Google DeepMind staff are quitting over military artificial intelligence work, with employees saying they're ashamed to work there. Confirmed by The Cool Down: the military deal raises ethics and oversight concerns.
Artificial intelligence agents show playful behavior on an island, and that playfulness boosts their performance on later tasks. Still open, per PCMag Australia: the agents like to play without any work assigned.
Grok and OpenAI's models show partisan bias when forced to choose between candidates during U.S. race analysis. Confirmed by Gadget Review: Grok picks Republicans while OpenAI picks Democrats.
The UK is committing £600M to counter artificial intelligence driven health and security threats, with major tech firms involved in the research projects. Confirmed by AI Insider: the allocation supports health, security and research.
Reservoir Media is suing Suno for 157.5m over 1,050 songs allegedly used in artificial intelligence training data. Still open, per PPC Land: the lawsuit centers on the training data copying claim.
Free every hour.
